summary: Local Axo control and event API between app/client and axod.
transport: Unix-domain socket at ~/Library/Application Support/Axo/run/axod.sock (override supported), mode 0600; per-user state defaults to ~/.axo/server.
framing: JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and responses are newline-delimited UTF-8; request line maximum 8 MiB, 64 requests in flight per connection. Concurrent responses may be out of order and correlate by JSON-RPC id.
version: axo.protocol.negotiate version 1; clients receive advertised method names, no other version is defined.

messages.name: axo.protocol.negotiate
messages.summary: Rejects unsupported protocol versions and returns the supported method list.

fields.name: maxEvents
fields.note: 1..=256; absent selects the legacy single-event result

returns.name: event or events
returns.note: Empty when poll times out; single-event or batch shape follows maxEvents presence.

fields.name: sequence
fields.note: Per-shell sequence starts at zero; repeated sequence is acknowledged and ignored.

messages.name: axo.session.event notification
messages.summary: Subscription-scoped notifications encode session.snapshot, session.removed, shell.activity, terminal.output, workspace.changed, session.focus, relay.status, or subscription.lagged; lag requires a new snapshot/list resynchronization.

messages.name: terminal.output
messages.summary: Base64 terminal output with per-shell sequence is streamed to subscribed clients that include streams; not a catalog event.

messages.name: axo.session.create / close; axo.shell.create / close; axo.session.layout.set
messages.summary: Create/close session and pane records and update validated session layout; close of final session creates a replacement.

messages.name: axo.workspace.*
messages.summary: List, create, rename, archive workspaces and create a session within a workspace.

messages.name: axo.relay.*
messages.summary: Read/configure/disable remote access, link host, read status, and request a connection.

parsing.summary: Typed method parameters deserialize from JSON before handlers execute; structs reject unknown fields, malformed values receive InvalidParams, while layout, terminal dimensions/input sequence and bounds are checked by handlers.

compatibility: Protocol negotiation currently accepts only version 1. Optional fields/defaults and the event poll's single-vs-batch response are explicit compatibility behaviors.
